sources: Dhaka Mahanagar Imarat Bidhimala 2025, Gazette 14 Dec 2025, pp. 13409–13519: Rules 41, 45, 47, 48, 53, 57, 59; Tables 1, 3, 5, 8, 10.

DAP 2022–2035 Volume I amendment, Bangladesh Gazette 14 Dec 2025, pp. 13385–13407: Article 3.6.4.1 (Base/Maximum FAR), Table 3.28 (incentive FAR), Table 3.29 (density), Appendix 3.6 (area FAR, density and units per katha for every block).
Verified page by page against the scanned book Bidhimala-2025-and-DAP-2022-2035.pdf (PDF pp. 46–80 and 117–138) on 2026-11-25.
notes: Area FAR comes from the block (DAP Appendix 3.6); Road FAR comes from Table 5 by occupancy, zone and road width (Rule 47(5)). Base FAR = lower of the two; Maximum FAR = higher (Rule 47(3), DAP 3.6.4.1(গ)). Incentives lift Base FAR toward Maximum FAR but never past it.

Table 5 band edges are exact metres (1.8, 2.5, 3.66, 4.88, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 m) stored in feet. Road FAR between two bands rises proportionally (Rule 47(6)). With a widening proposal, Road FAR is the average of existing and proposed road FAR (Rule 47(8)).
If Maximum FAR − Base FAR is 0.1 or less, Maximum FAR is granted without incentives (Rule 47(12)).
Incentive FAR is the sum of the automatic tiers (plot size, road width) plus the incentives the applicant selects. The sum is only usable up to Maximum FAR.
Plot-size tiers use the lower bound inclusively: 3–6 katha = 2,160 ≤ area < 4,320 sft (1 katha = 720 sft). Plots under 3 katha get no size incentive.

Road-width incentive: the reference text for DAP Table 3.28 row 2 is ambiguous. It is modelled as 0.02 FAR per foot above 30 ft, capped at 1.00 (reached at 80 ft), which matches the 'maximum 1, up to 80 ft' wording. It is 0.00 at 30 ft. Confirm against the gazette before relying on it for roads wider than 30 ft.
Green building: amount depends on the recognised certification, maximum 0.50. The default input is 0.50; lower it to the verified amount.
Floor area = (net plot area after road surrender + 3 × surrendered area) × applied FAR (Rule 48(2), (4); DAP 3.6.4.2). Without any surrender it is plot area × applied FAR.
Non-residential occupancies (groups B–K) use Road FAR only (Rule 47(4)); occupancies L and M have no Table 5 data and are not offered.
Where a plot has more than one adjoining road, the widest road governs (Rule 47(10)). A sub-divided plot's approvable FAR is 0.25 lower (Rule 51(10)).
Rule 47(3) allows up to 0.5 FAR above Maximum FAR for block-based development, urban regeneration and TDR; this is exposed as an approval-dependent input (dapExceptionalFarExcess).
TOD, TDR and FAR-purchase incentives have no fixed value in the reference; enter only an amount approved under the applicable guideline or notification.
Units per katha come from the selected block (DAP Appendix 3.6). Up to 10% more A3 units may be approved, never more floor area (DAP 3.6.4.1(ঘ)).

Not modelled from the book: the A6 6 ft minimum road (DAP 3.6.1), Rule 59(2) stretcher lift type, fire-stair rules (Appendix 1) and flood-flow zones where FAR and units are zero (Appendix 3.6 note 1).

Block boundaries are traced from the gazette density-block map (DAP Figure 3.14 as amended, Gazette 14 Dec 2025 p. 13392) and georeferenced on known planned areas; expect errors of about 0.7 km, up to 2 km at the edges. Block-19 (Korail) is not labelled on that map and keeps a point. Confirm any plot on the RAJUK masterplan.
